findings.description: D1 requires the backend to recompute and compare `routing_context_digest` before launch (`openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/design.md:27-33`), and the digest source is the full dg-06 `RoutingDispatchContext` including optional provenance and assignment extension fields (`design.md:27-29`; `openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/specs/vendor-dispatch/spec.md:31-32`; `openspec/changes/make-the-orchestrator-obey-the-router/contracts/routing-dispatch-context.schema.json:7-27,29-51`). Task 4.3 only embeds the closed `DispatchExecutionContext` projection plus digest (`openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/tasks.md:44-47`), and that schema forbids additional properties and omits provenance (`openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/contracts/dispatch-execution-context.schema.json:5-37`). The process backend therefore cannot reconstruct the digest input bytes from the carried context, so the immutability check is unimplementable as written. Carry the full digest-source document (or its canonical bytes) with the projection, or redefine the digest over only projection-carried fields and drop provenance/unprojected extensions from the digest contract.
findings.existing_code:
The digest source document is exactly the validated dg-06 `RoutingDispatchContext` contract:
`schema_version`, `decision_id`, `item_id`, `phase`, `attempt`, `dispatch_work_id`, the complete
assignment object (including extension fields and normalized `base_url`), and optional provenance.
Mutable lifecycle fields such as status and `prepared_at` are excluded. It is SHA-256 over UTF-8
canonical JSON with lexicographically sorted object keys, compact separators, and no floats. The
host computes it immediately after dg-06 validation; the backend recomputes and compares it before
launch.

findings.description: Local CLI process registration is still incomplete. `specs/vendor-dispatch/spec.md:3-11` requires every coordinator evaluation backend lifecycle command to use the shared backend and a maintained production-surface registry; D10 names only Claude Code, Codex, and Pi (`openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/design.md:262-266`); and `wp-vendor-wiring` write scope lists only those three modules (`openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/work-packages.yaml:179-181`). The landed evaluation roster also launches vendor CLIs from `agent-coordinator/evaluation/backends/antigravity.py:71-77` and `agent-coordinator/evaluation/backends/grok.py:121-128`, registered in `agent-coordinator/evaluation/backends/registry.py:25-31`. Those sinks remain outside package ownership, so either the AST/config guard fails on unowned files or the surfaces stay unsandboxed bypasses. Add antigravity and grok evaluation backends to D10, task 4.x coverage, and `wp-vendor-wiring` locks/write_allow, or explicitly classify them out of dg-07 with a matching registry exemption.
findings.existing_code:
The production process-surface registry includes review dispatcher submit/poll/repair/snapshot,
autopilot providers, `fact_check.py`, evaluation backends for Claude Code, Codex, and Pi,
quick-task, and phase-fixer mutation flows. Configuration validation requires every local CLI
surface to register.

findings.description: D3 requires backend-authored `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` so linked-worktree `git status` works under write-denied Git metadata (`openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/design.md:94-97`), but D5's positive child-environment allowlist enumerates only locale/terminal/time, HOME/XDG/temporary/PATH/proxy, and the lane credential (`design.md:148-151`) and does not include `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS`. Task 3.1 pins Git read/write behavior without naming the env var in the allowlist contract (`openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/tasks.md:24-27`). As written, a strict allowlist implementation drops the variable D3 depends on, so the Git status acceptance path fails after sandbox start. Add `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS` to the normative allowlist and to the child-env tests.
findings.existing_code:
System/runtime reads outside the user-home region are a documented residual. Tests cover `git
status` readability with backend-authored `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, denied Git mutation,
credential/sibling/arbitrary-home reads, and the
read-only common-git carve-out.

The child environment is constructed from a positive allowlist rather than copied from the
coordinator. It contains only safe locale/terminal/time variables (`LANG`, `LC_*`, `TERM`, `TZ`),
backend-authored `HOME`, XDG, temporary, `PATH`, and proxy variables, and the selected lane's
single authored credential key.

findings.description: D3 and task 4.1 treat per-lane `state_env_keys` as authored configuration that the backend projects into the ephemeral state root (`openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/design.md:73-74`; `openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/tasks.md:37-40`), but the landed `agents.yaml` CLI schema has no such field and rejects unknown keys (`agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py:476-539`, `CliConfig` at `574-595`). Task 4.1 says to "preserve" `state_env_keys` rather than add and validate it, so implementers have no schema, loader field, or fail-closed shape for the state-env projection D3 requires. Extend the CLI schema/`CliConfig` with `state_env_keys`, require it (or an explicit empty list) for sandbox-eligible lanes, and replace "preserve" with RED/GREEN coverage for missing keys and projection into the ephemeral root.
findings.existing_code:
Per-lane `state_env_keys` and credential environment keys are authored in `agents.yaml`; the
backend points only those state keys into the ephemeral root and no renderer hard-codes a vendor.

- [ ] 4.1 Test and fix config projection so effective mode isolation is mode override then entry,
  only for standalone calls; require each mode's explicit enforcement scope/write capability and
  preserve per-vendor `state_env_keys`/`api_key_env`/proxy-compatibility configuration; sandbox

findings.description: D4 claims a closed SRT-compatible DNS grammar and renderer tests that pin SRT 0.0.77 wildcard multi-label behavior (`openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/design.md:101-103,127-128`), but `network-policy-export.schema.json:28` uses a wildcard lookahead `(?=[^.]+\.[^.]+$)` that accepts only exactly two labels after `*.`. SRT 0.0.77 accepts any wildcard whose domain has `parts.length >= 2` (e.g. `*.foo.example.com`, `*.api.github.com`). Schema-valid exports therefore cannot carry SRT-valid multi-label wildcards, and an authored SRT-valid rule becomes unrenderable/fail-closed at the contract boundary. Widen the DNS pattern to SRT's `>= 2` parts rule (while still rejecting `*.com`), or document and test an intentional stricter subset.
